chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said:
I asked him about the man who divorces his wife while he is absent. He said: His divorce is valid in every state, and his wife observes the waiting period from the day he divorces her.
ai.seo_question: Is a divorce valid if the husband is absent when he pronounces it?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the validity of talaq al-gha'ib (divorce by the absentee), affirming that physical presence is not a prerequisite for the pronouncement to be legally binding. It establishes that the iddah (waiting period) commences from the day the divorce is effected, a ruling consistent with the broader Shia jurisprudential consensus on the efficacy of the husband's declaration regardless of his location.
